fields.claim_quote:
Let $G$ a group and $Z(G)$ the center of $G.$ The \emph{non-commuting graph} $\Gamma(G)$ associated to $G$
is the graph with vertex set $G \setminus Z(G)$ and such that two vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent
whenever $xy \neq yx$.

Let $G$ and $H$ be non-abelian finite groups and let $M(G)$ denote the set of orders
of maximal abelian subgroups of $G$. A subset of the vertices of a graph is called an \emph{independent set} if
its elements are pairwise non-adjacent and a subset of the vertices is a \emph{maximal
independent set} if it is maximal with respect to the inclusion.

Let $G$ be a non-commutative finite group, we define the \emph{independent polynomial of} $G$ as
\[Pi_G(x) = \sum_{i \geq 1} \mathrm{m.i.s} (G, i) x^i,\]
where $\mathrm{m.i.s} (G, i)$ is the number maximal independent sets of $V(\Gamma(G))$ of size $i.$

A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is termed \emph{maximal abelian subgroup} or a \emph{self-centralizing abelian subgroup} if it satisfies the following equivalent conditions:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $H=C_{G}(H)$, where $C_{G}(H)$ denotes the centralizer of $H$ in $G$;
  \item $C_{G}(H)H\leq H$ and $H$ is abelian;
  \item $H$ is abelian, and if $H\leq K\leq G$ with $K$ abelian, then $H=K$.
\end{itemize}

Let $G$ be a non-commutative finite group, we define the \emph{polynomial of maximal abelian subgroups of} $G$ as
\[PAS_G(x) = \sum_{i \geq 1} \mathrm{m.a.s} (G, i) x^i,\]
where $\mathrm{m.a.s} (G, i)$ is the number maximal abelian subgroups of $G$ of size $i.$

Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite group, then for all $m \geq |Z(G)|$ we have that $\mathrm{m.i.s}(G, m) = \mathrm{m.a.s}(G, m-|Z(G)|)$
fields.explanation: The original S3,m=1 witness is preserved. Mathlib Equiv.Perm(Fin3), Subgroup.center and the actual noncommuting SimpleGraph define the source objects. Library Maximal graph.IsIndepSet is converted to equivalent finite quantification solely to decide it, giving exactly three maximal singleton independent sets and one maximal two-element set. Actual maximal abelian Subgroup objects use Mathlib Maximal and IsMulCommutative. No subgroup has cardinality zero, so the printed m-minus-center-cardinality count is zero rather than three. Noncommutativity and center cardinality one satisfy the full source hypotheses. This is the local printed sign error, not a new group-theoretic target.
fields.flaw: Let G be a finite non-abelian group, let Z(G) denote its center, and let Γ(G) be the graph whose vertex set is G \ Z(G), with two vertices x and y adjacent exactly when xy ≠ yx. A subset of the vertices is independent when its elements are pairwise non-adjacent, and it is maximal independent when it is maximal under inclusion. For an integer i, let m.i.s.(G,i) be the number of maximal independent subsets of V(Γ(G)) having cardinality i. A subgroup H ≤ G is maximal abelian when H is abelian and every abelian subgroup K satisfying H ≤ K ≤ G equals H. Let m.a.s.(G,i) be the number of maximal abelian subgroups of G having cardinality i. Here |X| denotes cardinality, so m and all size indices are integers. The claim is: for every finite non-abelian group G and every integer m ≥ |Z(G)|, m.i.s.(G,m) = m.a.s.(G,m−|Z(G)|).
fields.problem: Title: Proof of a conjecture of Abdollahi-Akbari-Maimani concerning the non-commutative graph of finite groups
fields.witness: Take G=S₃={e,(12),(13),(23),(123),(132)} and m=1. G is finite non-abelian and Z(G)={e}, so m≥|Z(G)|. In Γ(G), each transposition commutes with no other vertex, while (123) and (132) commute. Hence the maximal independent sets are {(12)}, {(13)}, {(23)}, and {(123),(132)}. Thus m.i.s.(G,1)=3. But m−|Z(G)|=0, and no subgroup has cardinality 0, so m.a.s.(G,0)=0.
